title: Palay Drawing: How to Draw Palay in Six Easy Steps, With Pictures
metaTitle: Palay Drawing: Easy Steps, Parts, Colors and a Free PNG
metaDescription: An easy palay drawing in six steps with pictures, the parts of the rice plant in English and Tagalog, coloring tips, a cartoon and a free palay PNG.
excerpt: To draw palay, start with the ground and roots. Then add six thin stems, long arching leaves, drooping panicle stems and many small oval grains. This palay drawing guide shows each step in a picture, names the parts in English and Tagalog, and gives you a free PNG for school. anee.io, a farm app for Filipino farmers, drew every picture here.

heroImage.alt: Palay drawing in color beside its pencil sketch: a rice plant with green leaves, golden drooping panicles and roots in brown soil

blocks.text: The palay plant in English is the rice plant, and palay also means its grain still in the hull. Our [palay guide](/crops/palay) explains the word in full. For this drawing you only need a pencil, an eraser, paper and some colors.

items: A rice plant is a clump of thin stems with long, narrow leaves and drooping heads of grain.
Draw it in six steps: ground and roots, stems, leaves, panicle stems, grains, then details.
Color the leaves in two greens and the grains golden yellow.
Save the free palay PNG and the palay cartoon for school use.

blocks.text: What are the parts of the palay plant?
Every rice plant has the same parts, and each one has a shape you can copy. The drawing below names them in English, with the Tagalog word in brackets.

blocks.alt: Labeled palay drawing showing the panicle, grains, flag leaf, leaf blade, leaf sheath, stem, tillers and roots of a rice plant
blocks.caption: The parts of the rice plant, with the Tagalog names farmers use. Drawing by anee.io.
Each part of the palay plant and how to draw it
rows: Thin lines spreading under the soil
A thin tube carrying leaves and panicle
A sleeve wrapped around the stem
Long, narrow and pointed, arching out
The short top leaf under the panicle
The head that bends over as grains fill

blocks.text: IRRI, the International Rice Research Institute, records these parts in its Standard Evaluation System for Rice. It sorts the panicle axis as straight or droopy and the flag leaf from erect to descending, so a drooping head beside an upright flag leaf is true to life. It also calls 10 to 19 tillers per plant a medium count, so six stems make a fair, simple clump. For more farm words, see our [English Tagalog farm glossary](/blog/farm-words-in-tagalog).
How do I make an easy palay drawing, step by step?
Sketch with light pencil lines so you can erase. In each picture, gray lines show what you already drew and dark lines show the new step.
Step 1: Draw the ground and the roots
Draw a long, gentle curve for the ground and round it off below like a bowl of soil. Then, from the middle, draw eight or nine thin roots that spread down and out.

blocks.alt: Step 1 of an easy palay drawing: the ground line, a clump of soil and thin roots
blocks.caption: Step 1: the ground and the roots.

blocks.text: Step 2: Draw the stems, or tillers
From that same point, draw six thin stems that fan out like an open hand. Keep the middle ones nearly straight, and wrap the base with a short sleeve so the stems look bundled.

blocks.alt: Step 2 of the palay drawing: six thin stems fanning out from one base
blocks.caption: Step 2: six tillers from one base.

blocks.text: Step 3: Draw the leaves and the flag leaves

Rice leaves are long, narrow and pointed. Start each one at a stem, follow the stem up a little, then let it arch out and down to a sharp tip. After that, add a short flag leaf near the top of the middle stems, pointing up.

blocks.alt: Step 3 of the palay drawing: long arching leaves and upright flag leaves added to the stems
blocks.caption: Step 3: long leaves and the flag leaves.

blocks.text: Step 4: Draw the drooping panicle stems
At the top of each stem, draw a panicle stem that rises a little, bends over like a hook and droops to the side. Next, hang five to seven short branches from it.

blocks.alt: Step 4 of the palay drawing: curved panicle stems with short branches drooping to the sides
blocks.caption: Step 4: the panicle stems bend over and droop.

blocks.text: Step 5: Draw the grains
Now add small ovals along each branch and down to the tip, packed close on both sides. This step turns your sketch into palay, so take your time.

blocks.alt: Step 5 of the palay drawing: many small oval grains along each drooping panicle
blocks.caption: Step 5: many small oval grains.

blocks.text: Step 6: Add the finishing details
Finish with a line down each leaf, a small band where each leaf starts and a short line on every grain. Some ripples of water show that palay grows in a flooded field.

blocks.alt: Step 6 of the palay drawing: leaf midribs, nodes, grain lines, pebbles and water added
blocks.caption: Step 6: the finishing details. Your palay drawing is done.

blocks.title: Make the heads heavy
blocks.text: If your drawing looks like grass, add more grains and bend the heads lower. Farmers read heads too: PhilRice's PalayCheck calls a white panicle with empty grains whitehead, a sign of [rice stem borer](/pests/rice-stem-borer). Golden and heavy means a good harvest.
Palay drawing with color: which colors should I use?
Use two greens for the leaves and golden yellow for the panicles and grains. If you only have a few crayons, color one half of each leaf darker, so the leaves look round instead of flat.

blocks.caption: A simple color guide for a palay drawing with color
rows: Shade one half of each leaf

blocks.text:
Golden yellow is the true color of ripe palay. PhilRice's PalayCheck System advises harvesting by hand when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, so a few greenish grains look real. Still, the IRRI guide lists hulls from straw and gold to brown, purple and black, so check a photo before you draw a special variety.

For a palay painting in watercolor or poster paint, lay down the light green first, then add the dark green once it dries.

blocks.text: How do I draw a palay cartoon?

Keep the same parts but make them round and simple: a plump green body for the stems, a fan of wide leaves and three panicles with chunky grains. Then put a face on the body with dark eyes, pink cheeks and a small smile. Thick outlines help it read from across a room.

blocks.alt: Palay cartoon: a cute rice plant with a smiling face, arching leaves and golden panicles on a mound of soil
blocks.caption: A palay cartoon by anee.io, free for school use. [Open the PNG file](/images/site/guides/palay-drawing/cartoon.png) for a clear background.

blocks.text: If you look for palay cartoon images online, check who owns each one before you print it.
Ideas for a palay poster, props, costume or background
A palay poster
Put a big palay drawing on one side and your title on the other, then label the parts like the diagram above. For a story to go with it, read the [Alamat ng Palay](/blog/alamat-ng-palay).
Palay props for a school program
Palay props are easy to make from cardboard and colored paper.

items.title: Trace
items.text: Print the color drawing or the cartoon and trace it on cardboard.

items.title: Cut
items.text: Cut around it with a small border so thin leaves do not tear.

items.title: Color
items.text: Paint it, or glue the printed picture on top.

items.title: Mount
items.text: Glue yellow paper ovals on the panicles, then tape a stick to the back.

blocks.text: A palay festival costume

When a school program calls for a palay festival costume, build it from the same parts. First, make a headband or hat with paper panicles drooping from it. Next, add a cape of long green paper leaves. Finally, wear a sash dotted with golden paper grains.
A palay background, a palayan drawing or a logo

For a palay background, draw rows of small clumps that shrink toward the horizon. A full palayan drawing, a rice field with dikes and mountains, is on our [Palayan, Nueva Ecija](/blog/palayan-nueva-ecija) page. For a palay logo, use one panicle and one leaf, since fewer lines print better small. And for an animated palay, put the six step pictures on six slides and click through them.

If your family grows the real crop, see our guide to [pagtatanim ng palay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-palay), or the [growth stages tool](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) in anee.io.
Questions about palay drawing

items.q: What is the palay plant in English?
items.a: The palay plant in English is the rice plant. Palay also means the grain still in its hull, called paddy or rough rice.

items.q: Can I use these palay drawings for school?
items.a: Yes. anee.io made every drawing here, and you may save and use them free for school work, posters and props.
Growing palay looks green, and the grains turn golden yellow as they ripen. Some varieties have brown, purple or black hulls.

items.q: What are the parts of the rice plant in Tagalog?
items.a: Roots are ugat, the stem is tangkay, tillers are suwi, a leaf is dahon, the panicle is uhay and a grain is butil. The hull is ipa.
